Investing.com — U.S. wireless carriers have spent the autumn on the wrong side of the market's hunt for safety. SpaceX's $8 billion deal for Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum, landing days after FCC approval for up to 15,000 Starlink mobile satellites, knocked AT&T (NYSE:T) and Verizon (NYSE:VZ) down about 10% each on October 9. T-Mobile US (NASDAQ:TMUS)—the 5G network leader—fell hardest that day, tumbling 13.2%, and has slipped 4.1% in the past week to $164.02, leaving it up just 5.1% over the past month.

The low multiple makes T-Mobile look like a mispriced defensive stock, but the discount reflects a debt-heavy carrier facing a well-funded new rival. At 15.4 times trailing earnings, with a 2.9% dividend yield, 31.4% forecast EPS growth, and 7.4% forecast revenue growth, T-Mobile has the numbers of a bargain, and InvestingPro's valuation models even flag it as "Undervalued" at $226.48, a 38.1% implied upside. But a capital-intensive balance sheet carrying 40.1% total debt-to-capital leaves less room for error as SpaceX moves into the wireless market.

Identifying when leverage turns a new competitor into a bigger threat is what ProPicks AI is built for. In Top Value and Dominate the Dow, InvestingPro's large-cap strategies built around cleaner balance sheets, T-Mobile was left out for November in favor of lower-leverage names—including communications companies with lighter debt loads and blue-chip cash generators.

See the lower-debt blue-chip leaders ProPicks AI holds instead: Explore the Top Value & Dow strategies on InvestingPro

The Network That Wins the Premium Customer

T-Mobile makes its money selling premium wireless plans, and network speed is its pricing power: median network speeds run 60% to 70% faster than competitors', according to Ookla data. The lead is pulling customers up the price ladder. Sixty percent of new lines now land on premium plans, customers porting in carry ARPAs 20% higher than those porting out, and postpaid ARPA grew 4% year-over-year.

Third-quarter results proved the premium strategy is working. Adjusted EPS of $3.22 topped the $2.89 consensus by 11.4%, and revenue of $23.58 billion beat the $23.15 billion forecast. Postpaid service revenue climbed 9% year-over-year, core adjusted EBITDA expanded 11%, and postpaid net account additions reached 274,000, with management guiding to about 1 million for the full year—above peak Un-carrier era levels. Management raised full-year guidance across the board, including adjusted free cash flow of $18.7 billion to $18.8 billion.

How Many Shares of AT&T, Verizon or Comcast Pay $1,000 a Month in Dividends? ©Whitestudio2015 from Getty Images, Adam Simpson from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

At today's prices, $1,000 a month in dividends takes about $195,600 of Verizon, about $229,500 of Comcast or about $237,300 of AT&T.

Verizon's 6.1% yield makes its check the cheapest of the three, and it's the one I'd want.

Verizon pays out 52% of its free cash flow, the most of the three, which still leaves plenty of room.

Comcast covers its dividend best but hasn't set a dividend policy for its split into two companies, and AT&T plans to hold its dividend flat.

Any retiree hunting for dividend income ends up looking at AT&T (T:NYSE), Verizon Communications (VZ:NYSE) and Comcast (CMCSA:NASDAQ) sooner or later, since all three yield more than 5% at today's prices.

But a $1,000-a-month dividend check costs a very different amount from each, and the checks aren't equally safe. Here's what $12,000 a year takes from each stock on its own:

Source: TIKR and StockAnalysis, at today's prices. Shares rounded up to whole shares. The payout ratio is dividends paid as a share of free cash flow over the 12 months to Sept. 30, 2026, and on fiscal 2026 consensus estimates.

6 safe dividend stocks paying retirees 6%+ yields

There are over 100 stocks paying 6%+ annual dividends today.

But after an extensive investment review leveraging TIKR's proprietary data, we now believe only six of them are truly safe for retirees.

They're all yours as part of our new investment report. Learn more about how to get access right here.

AT&T's check is safe, and staying put

AT&T asks the most: about 10,811 shares, or about $237,300, for a 5.1% yield. And the check won't grow. AT&T plans to hold its dividend at $1.11 a share a year, down from $2.08 in fiscal 2020. Free cash flow has covered the smaller dividend with plenty to spare:

AT&T (T): free cash flow vs. dividends paid, $ billions, fiscal 2016–2025 (TIKR)

The dividend took 44% of free cash flow over the 12 months to Sept. 30, with 46% expected for fiscal 2026. AT&T guides to $18 billion or more of free cash flow in 2026 and $21 billion or more in 2028.

The risk is debt. After AT&T's $23 billion spectrum purchase from EchoStar, its net debt rose to 3.13x adjusted EBITDA at the end of September from 2.68x at the end of June, and the company doesn't expect to get back to its 2.5x target until 2029.

Verizon is the cheapest check, and still growing

Verizon takes the fewest dollars: about 4,241 shares, or about $195,600, at a 6.1% yield. That's about $41,700 less than AT&T for the same $1,000 a month. Its dividend took 52% of free cash flow over the 12 months to Sept. 30, with 53% expected for fiscal 2026, and the ratio fell from 76.9% in fiscal 2022 to 57.0% in fiscal 2025 as free cash flow grew from $14.1 billion to $20.1 billion:

AST SpaceMobile Sinks 8% as New Offering Filing Revives Dilution Fears ©@Seasonal via Canva, @Oleksii Mach via Canva
Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile fell 8% today after a new filing, its second in two days, pointed to another securities sale.

Selling stock near a 52-week low is the costliest way to fund the build-out.

The diluted share count rose from 200 million to 300 million between late 2024 and the third quarter of 2026.

AT&T and Vodafone need the satellites funded, and a launch date for BlueBirds 14 to 16 is the next test.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) sank 8% today on a filing that points to more dilution. The news reaches AT&T (T:NYSE) and Vodafone (VOD) too, which sell AST's coverage to their subscribers and own stakes in the company.

On Tuesday morning, a prospectus supplement covered 10 million Class A shares AST issued to Firefly Aerospace. After Tuesday's close, an 8-K added a legal opinion, usually a sign of a securities sale. Then, before today's open, AST filed a new supplement covering [THE OFFERING'S TYPE AND SIZE, FROM THE 424B5].

AT&T generated $5.0 billion of free cash flow in the third quarter, so a smaller AST stake barely registers. A stalled constellation would matter far more now that SpaceX is buying spectrum for phone service of its own. Vodafone, AST's partner in a European satellite venture, just raised its fiscal 2027 adjusted free cash flow guidance to €2.8 billion to €3.0 billion.

The bill keeps growing

Free cash flow came to about -$1.8 billion over the last four quarters, against $3.2 billion of cash. Analysts expect free cash flow to stay negative through 2028, while revenue climbs from $70.9 million in 2025 to $1.65 billion:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

The 2027 estimate has already fallen to $586 million, from $748 million at the end of June.

TIKR tracks 13 analysts on AST SpaceMobile. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on AST SpaceMobile, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See AST SpaceMobile's Analyst Ratings

Selling low costs more shares

The share count has grown by half in under two years:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): diluted shares outstanding, millions of shares, last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)

The count flattened in 2026 as AST leaned on convertible notes, including July's $1.15 billion, which convert at about $80 a share. At today's price, a new share brings in about a third of that. Forward price/sales was 21x at the last close, against a five-year average of 60x:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's drop takes it lower still, to about 19x. Another raise was always coming, and I'd expect AST to keep selling stock until launches pick up. BlueBirds 14 to 16 still don't have a launch date, and the target for about 45 satellites has slipped to mid-2027. Fourth-quarter results early next year need a firm launch schedule and 2026 revenue inside the $150 million to $200 million guidance.

AT&T: Gradual Upward Revenue Growth Trends

AT&T (NYSE:T) primarily generates its revenue by providing wireless voice and data communication networks, broadband fiber optic internet access, and customized cybersecurity and cloud-based solutions to a diverse base of multinational corporations, small businesses, and individual residential consumers.

It recently announced an official agreement to sell its Mexican regional business unit to Grupo Televisa (NYSE:TV) and Fintech Holdings, and it also broke ground on a new global corporate headquarters campus located in Plano, Texas.

Verizon Communications: Maintaining Stable Total Revenue Figures

Verizon Communications (NYSE:VZ) earns the majority of its revenue by delivering subscription-based mobile wireless service plans, residential fixed broadband internet connectivity, and broad private networking and unified collaboration platforms to individual customers, global enterprise organizations, and government agencies.

It formally expanded a strategic technology infrastructure partnership with Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and its Amazon Web Services arm to build new data network capabilities, while it simultaneously commenced a phased regional shutdown of its older legacy copper telephone and internet service lines.
